title: Frequency Spread
description: Count how many times each distinct value occurs in `nums`. Return the highest count minus the lowest count.

examples.explanation: The spread between highest and lowest count is 1.
The spread between highest and lowest count is 0.

title: Adjacent Equal Pair Count
description: Return the number of indices `i` with `0 <= i < nums.length - 1` such that `nums[i] == nums[i + 1]`.

title: Even Prefix Sum Count
description: A prefix is the first `k` elements for `1 <= k <= nums.length`. Return how many prefixes have an even sum.

title: Most Common Digit
description: Write every number of `nums` in decimal (ignore minus signs) and count how often each digit `0-9` appears overall. Return the digit that appears most often; on a tie return the smaller digit.

title: Clamped Array Total
description: Replace every element `x` of `nums` by `lo` if `x < lo`, by `hi` if `x > hi`, and keep it otherwise. Return the sum of the resulting array.

title: Index Parity Agreement
description: Count the indices `i` (0-based) for which `nums[i]` and `i` have the same parity (both even or both odd).

title: Halves Sum Difference
description: Split `nums` into a left half (first `n / 2` elements), a right half (last `n / 2` elements, integer division) and, for odd `n`, a middle element which is ignored. Return the absolute difference between the left and right sums.

title: Widest Gap Between Targets
description: Look at the positions where `target` occurs in `nums`. Return the largest difference between two consecutive occurrences, or `0` if it occurs fewer than two times.

title: Median Triple Total
description: For every window of three consecutive elements of `nums` take its median (the middle value when sorted). Return the sum of these medians (`0` if `nums` has fewer than 3 elements).

title: Binary Search Probe Count
description: Run the standard binary search for `target` on the sorted array `nums` (`mid = (lo + hi) / 2` with integer division, `lo = 0`, `hi = n - 1`, shrinking to `mid + 1` or `mid - 1`). Return how many middle elements are inspected before it stops, whether or not the target is found.
constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 1000, nums is sorted ascending with distinct values

title: Above Average Count
description: Return how many elements of `nums` are strictly greater than the average of the whole array (compare exactly, do not round the average).

title: Vowel Consonant Gap
description: `s` contains only lowercase letters. Return the absolute difference between the number of vowels (`a e i o u`) and the number of consonants.

title: Uppercase Letter Count
description: Return how many characters of `s` are uppercase letters (`A-Z`). `s` may also contain lowercase letters and digits.

title: Same End Letter Words
description: `s` is a sentence of lowercase words separated by single spaces. Return how many words start and end with the same letter (a one-letter word counts).
constraints: words are lowercase and separated by exactly one space

title: Digit Character Sum
description: `s` contains letters and digits. Return the sum of the digit characters (each digit counts as its numeric value; letters count as `0`).

title: Strict Case Alternation
description: `s` contains only letters. Return `true` if the letters alternate strictly between uppercase and lowercase from one position to the next (starting with either case).

title: Shared Prefix Length
description: Return the length of the longest common prefix of the strings `a` and `b` (`0` if their first characters differ).

title: Vowel Position Sum
description: Positions in `s` are numbered from `1`. Return the sum of the positions at which a vowel (`a e i o u`) appears.

examples.explanation: The vowel positions add up to 7.
The vowel positions add up to 1.

title: Character Run Count
description: A run is a maximal block of identical consecutive characters. Return the number of runs in `s`.

title: Runner-Up Letter
description: Rank the letters of `s` by how often they occur (more occurrences first; equal counts ordered alphabetically). Return the letter ranked second.
constraints: lowercase letters; at least two different letters appear

title: Average Word Length Floor
description: `s` is a sentence of lowercase words separated by single spaces. Return the average word length rounded down.
constraints: words are lowercase and separated by exactly one space

title: Ones Block Count
description: `s` is a binary string. Return the number of maximal blocks of consecutive `1` characters.

title: Cross Array Pair Sum
description: Return `true` if one element of `a` and one element of `b` add up to `target`.

title: Rising Day Count
description: `prices[i]` is the price on day `i`. Return the number of days `i >= 1` on which the price is strictly higher than on day `i - 1`.

title: Total Travel Distance
description: A traveller visits the positions listed in `stops` in order. Return the total distance travelled, i.e. the sum of `|stops[i + 1] - stops[i]|`.

title: Dominant Parity
description: Return `1` if `nums` contains more odd numbers than even numbers, `0` if it contains more even numbers, and `-1` if the counts are equal.

title: Busiest Tens Bucket
description: Group the numbers of `nums` into buckets by `x / 10` (integer division): bucket `0` holds 0-9, bucket `1` holds 10-19, and so on. Return the index of the fullest bucket; on a tie return the smaller index.

title: Values In Range Count
description: Return how many elements of `nums` lie in the inclusive range `[lo, hi]`.

title: Extreme Index Distance
description: Let `i` be the index of the first occurrence of the maximum of `nums` and `j` the index of the first occurrence of the minimum. Return `|i - j|`.

title: Consecutive Rise Triples
description: Count the indices `i` with `nums[i] < nums[i + 1] < nums[i + 2]`.

title: Same Multiset Check
description: Return `true` if arrays `a` and `b` contain exactly the same values with the same multiplicities (order does not matter).

title: First Repeat Position
description: Scan `nums` from left to right and return the index of the first element whose value has already appeared earlier, or `-1` if all values are distinct.

examples.explanation: The first repeat is at index 2 (-1 means none).
The first repeat is at index -1 (-1 means none).

title: Running Maximum Total
description: For each index `i`, let `m[i]` be the largest value among `nums[0..i]`. Return the sum of all `m[i]`.

examples.explanation: The running maxima add up to 7.
The running maxima add up to 5.

title: Net Zero Check
description: Return `true` if the elements of `nums` add up to exactly zero.

title: Widest Word In Sentence
description: `s` is a sentence of lowercase words separated by single spaces. Return the length of the longest word.
constraints: words are lowercase and separated by exactly one space

title: Equal Digit Sum Pairs
description: Count the pairs of indices `i < j` for which `nums[i]` and `nums[j]` have the same sum of decimal digits.

title: Power Of Two Sum Pairs
description: Count the pairs of indices `i < j` for which `nums[i] + nums[j]` is a power of two (`1, 2, 4, 8, ...`).

examples.explanation: 3 pair(s) add up to a power of two.
0 pair(s) add up to a power of two.

title: Most Distinct After Shifts
description: You may add to every element of `nums` one integer from `-k` to `k` (each element chooses its own shift). Return the largest possible number of distinct values in the resulting array.

examples.explanation: At most 6 distinct value(s) are possible.
At most 3 distinct value(s) are possible.

title: Next Greater Frequency Total
description: Let `f(x)` be how many times value `x` occurs in the whole array. For each index `i` find the nearest index `j > i` with `f(nums[j]) > f(nums[i])` and take `nums[j]`; if no such index exists take `-1`. Return the sum of the values taken.

examples.explanation: The chosen values add up to 1.
The chosen values add up to -1.

title: Same Value Distance Total
description: For every index `i`, add up `|i - j|` over all other indices `j` with `nums[j] == nums[i]`. Return the sum of these totals over all `i`.

title: Max Chunks With Duplicates
description: Split `nums` into the largest number of contiguous chunks so that sorting each chunk on its own and joining the chunks in order gives the fully sorted array. Return that largest number of chunks (values may repeat).

examples.explanation: The array can be cut into 1 chunk(s).
The array can be cut into 4 chunk(s).

title: Subarrays With Frequent Maximum
description: Let `M` be the largest value in the whole array. Count the contiguous subarrays in which `M` occurs at least `k` times.

title: Reverse-Sum Twin Pairs
description: Let `rev(x)` be `x` with its decimal digits reversed (`120` becomes `21`). Count the pairs `i < j` with `nums[i] + rev(nums[j]) == nums[j] + rev(nums[i])`.

title: First Unformable Total
description: Return the smallest positive integer that cannot be written as the sum of some sub-collection of `nums` (each element used at most once; the collection may be a single element).

title: Block Up The Ones Swaps
description: `bits` is a binary array. A swap exchanges the values at any two positions. Return the minimum number of swaps needed so that all `1` values form one contiguous block (`0` if there are no ones).

title: Polygon Doubled Area
description: `points` lists, as flat pairs `[x0, y0, x1, y1, ...]`, the vertices of a simple polygon in order (clockwise or counter-clockwise). Return twice the polygon's area, which is always an integer.
constraints: -100 <= x, y <= 100; the polygon does not cross itself and has non-zero area

title: Point Inside Polygon
description: `points` lists, as flat pairs, the vertices of a simple polygon in order. Return `true` if the point `(qx, qy)` lies inside the polygon or exactly on its boundary.
constraints: -100 <= x, y, qx, qy <= 100; the polygon is simple with non-zero area

title: Most Points On One Line
description: `points` lists distinct points as flat pairs `[x0, y0, x1, y1, ...]`. Return the largest number of points that lie on a single straight line.
constraints: -1000 <= x, y <= 1000; all points are distinct

title: Equidistant Pair Count
description: `points` lists distinct points as flat pairs. Count the ordered triples `(i, j, k)` of different points where point `j` and point `k` are at the same distance from point `i` (swapping `j` and `k` counts as a different triple).
constraints: -1000 <= x, y <= 1000; all points are distinct

title: Four Points Make Square
description: `points` holds exactly four points as flat pairs `[x0, y0, ..., x3, y3]` in any order. Return `true` if they are the corners of a square (non-zero side length).

title: Convex Polygon Check
description: `points` lists the vertices of a simple polygon in order as flat pairs. Return `true` if the polygon is convex (every turn goes the same direction; vertices lying on a straight line with their neighbours are allowed).
constraints: -100 <= x, y <= 100; the polygon is simple with non-zero area

title: Overlapping Rectangle Pairs
description: `rects` lists axis-aligned rectangles as flat quadruples `[x1, y1, x2, y2, ...]` (bottom-left `(x1, y1)`, top-right `(x2, y2)`, with `x1 < x2` and `y1 < y2`). Count the pairs of rectangles whose overlap has positive area (touching along an edge or at a corner does not count).

title: Closest Pair Squared Distance
description: `points` lists at least two distinct points as flat pairs. Return the smallest squared Euclidean distance `(dx * dx + dy * dy)` between any two different points.
constraints: -10^4 <= x, y <= 10^4; all points are distinct

title: Cell Cluster Perimeter
description: `cells` lists distinct unit squares of the plane as flat pairs `[x0, y0, ...]` (the square with lower-left corner `(x, y)`). Return the total length of the boundary of the shape formed by their union, counting every unit edge that separates a chosen square from an unchosen one (this includes edges around holes).
constraints: -1000 <= x, y <= 1000; all cells are distinct

title: Rectangle Union Area
description: `rects` lists axis-aligned rectangles as flat quadruples `[x1, y1, x2, y2, ...]` with `x1 < x2` and `y1 < y2`. Return the total area covered by at least one rectangle (overlapping regions are counted once).

examples.explanation: The union covers an area of 7.
The union covers an area of 1.

title: Perfect Rectangle Cover
description: `rects` lists axis-aligned rectangles as flat quadruples `[x1, y1, x2, y2, ...]` with `x1 < x2` and `y1 < y2`. Return `true` if together they cover one single rectangle exactly, with no gaps and no overlaps.

title: Right Triangle Count
description: `points` lists distinct points as flat pairs. Count the sets of three points that form a triangle with a right angle at one of its corners (the three points must not lie on one line).
constraints: -1000 <= x, y <= 1000; all points are distinct

title: Parallelogram Count
description: `points` lists distinct points as flat pairs. Count the sets of four points that are the corners of a parallelogram with non-zero area (rectangles, rhombuses and squares count too).
constraints: -1000 <= x, y <= 1000; all points are distinct

title: Smallest Axis Rectangle Area
description: `points` lists distinct points as flat pairs. Return the smallest area of an axis-parallel rectangle whose four corners are all in `points`, or `0` if no such rectangle exists.
constraints: 0 <= x, y <= 10^4; all points are distinct

title: Axis Square Count
description: `points` lists distinct points as flat pairs. Count the axis-parallel squares (positive side length, sides parallel to the x and y axes) whose four corners are all in `points`.
constraints: 0 <= x, y <= 100; all points are distinct

title: Meeting Spot Manhattan Cost
description: Friends live at the points listed in `points` (flat pairs, repeats allowed). They meet at an integer point and each walks along the grid, so the distance is `|dx| + |dy|`. Return the smallest possible total walking distance over all meeting points.

title: Vertical Mirror Symmetry
description: `points` lists distinct points as flat pairs. Return `true` if there is a vertical line `x = c` (c may be a half-integer) such that reflecting every point across it gives back exactly the same set of points.
constraints: -1000 <= x, y <= 1000; all points are distinct

title: Days Between Two Dates
description: Given two calendar dates `(y1, m1, d1)` and `(y2, m2, d2)` in the Gregorian calendar, return the number of days between them (always non-negative; the same date gives `0`). A year is a leap year if divisible by 4, except years divisible by 100 that are not divisible by 400.
constraints: both dates are valid; either date may come first

title: Friday The Thirteenth Count
description: Return how many months in the years `a` to `b` inclusive have their 13th day on a Friday (Gregorian calendar; 1 January 1900 was a Monday).
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Repeating Decimal Period
description: Write the fraction `p / q` as a decimal. Return the length of its repeating cycle (for example `1/3 = 0.333...` has length `1`, `1/7` has length `6`), or `0` if the decimal terminates.
constraints: the fraction need not be in lowest terms

title: Digit At Sequence Position
description: Write the positive integers one after another to form the digit stream `1234567891011121314...`. Return the digit at position `n` (positions start at `1`).

examples.explanation: The digit at that position is 3.
The digit at that position is 0.

constraints: the answer is a single digit 0-9

title: Smallest Repunit Base
description: A repunit is a number whose digits are all `1`. Return the smallest base `k >= 2` in which `n` is written as a repunit with at least two digits (such a base always exists: `n - 1`).

title: Spelled Number Letters
description: Write each number from `1` to `n` in British English words, for example `342` is `three hundred and forty-two`, `115` is `one hundred and fifteen` and `1000` is `one thousand`. A word like `and` is inserted after `hundred` or `thousand` whenever something less than a hundred follows. Hyphens and spaces are not counted. Return the total number of letters used for all the numbers.
constraints: use the style shown: `nine thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine`

title: Balanced Ternary Length
description: Balanced ternary writes integers with the digits `-1, 0, 1` (powers of 3 as place values) and no leading zeros. Return how many digits the balanced ternary form of `n` needs (`0` needs `1` digit).

examples.explanation: The balanced ternary form has 1 digit(s).
The balanced ternary form has 1 digit(s).

constraints: the sign does not change the length

title: Traffic Light Wait Total
description: A light starts green at second `0`; it stays green for `g` seconds, then red for `red` seconds, and repeats. A car arriving at second `t` drives through at once if the light is green (green covers seconds `0..g-1` of each cycle), otherwise it waits until the next green. Return the total waiting seconds of all cars in `times`.

examples.explanation: The cars wait 3 second(s) in total.
The cars wait 0 second(s) in total.

title: Dominoes Final State
description: `s` describes a row of dominoes: `L` is pushed left, `R` is pushed right, `.` stands upright. Every second each falling domino topples its upright neighbour in the direction it falls, but an upright domino hit from both sides at the same second stays upright. Return the final row once nothing changes.

title: Duration String Seconds
description: A duration is written as a sequence of `<number><unit>` parts, where the unit is `d` (86400 seconds), `h` (3600), `m` (60) or `s` (1), for example `1h30m5s`. Units may repeat or appear in any order. Return the total number of seconds.
constraints: each number has 1 to 4 digits; only the letters d, h, m, s are used as units

title: Curly Brace Reversals
description: `s` contains only `{` and `}`. In one operation you flip a single brace into the other kind. Return the minimum operations needed to make `s` a balanced sequence, or `-1` if that is impossible.

title: Bracket Pair Span Total
description: `s` is a balanced string of round brackets. Every `(` is matched with its closing `)`. For each matched pair take the distance between the two positions (closing index minus opening index). Return the sum of these distances.

examples.explanation: The pair spans add up to 1.
The pair spans add up to 4.

constraints: s is a balanced sequence of ( and )

title: Pyramid Cup Fill Level
description: Cups are stacked in a pyramid: row `r` has `r + 1` cups, and cup `(r, k)` sits above cups `(r + 1, k)` and `(r + 1, k + 1)`. Each cup holds `c` units. `p` units are poured into the top cup; whatever a full cup cannot hold overflows, split equally between the two cups below it (overflow is exact, fractions allowed). Return the number of whole units in cup `(row, col)` (round down).

title: Convex Hull Doubled Area
description: `points` lists distinct points as flat pairs. Imagine a rubber band stretched around all of them (the convex hull). Return twice the area enclosed by it, or `0` if all points lie on one line or there are fewer than three points.
constraints: -1000 <= x, y <= 1000; all points are distinct

title: Largest Triangle Doubled Area
description: `points` lists distinct points as flat pairs. Among all triangles whose corners are three of the points, return twice the area of the largest one (`0` if fewer than three points or all collinear).
constraints: -1000 <= x, y <= 1000; all points are distinct

title: Rectangle Union Perimeter
description: `rects` lists axis-aligned rectangles as flat quadruples `[x1, y1, x2, y2, ...]` with `x1 < x2` and `y1 < y2`. Return the total length of the outline of their union (including the outlines of any holes).

title: Most Points In Square Window
description: `points` lists distinct points as flat pairs. A square window `[x, x + k] x [y, y + k]` (borders included, `x` and `y` any integers) is placed on the plane. Return the largest number of points it can contain.

examples.explanation: A window can hold at most 2 point(s).
A window can hold at most 1 point(s).

constraints: -1000 <= x, y <= 1000, 0 <= k <= 2000; all points are distinct

title: Interior Lattice Points
description: `points` lists the vertices of a simple polygon in order as flat pairs. Return how many integer points lie strictly inside the polygon (points on its boundary are not counted).
constraints: -100 <= x, y <= 100; the polygon is simple with non-zero area

title: Tilted Rectangle Count
description: `points` lists distinct points as flat pairs. Count the sets of four points that are the corners of a rectangle with non-zero area; the rectangle may be rotated to any angle and squares count.
constraints: -1000 <= x, y <= 1000; all points are distinct

title: Next Palindromic Date
description: A date is palindromic if its `YYYYMMDD` digits read the same backwards (for example `20211202`). Given a valid date, return the first palindromic date strictly after it, as the integer `YYYYMMDD`.
constraints: the input date is valid (Gregorian calendar)

title: Shortest Zero-One Multiple
description: Find the smallest positive multiple of `n` whose decimal digits are all `0` or `1` and return how many digits it has (for `n = 3` the multiple is `111`, so the answer is `3`).
constraints: a multiple with digits 0 and 1 always exists

title: Smallest Number After K Swaps
description: `num` is a string of decimal digits (leading zeros allowed). In one move you swap two neighbouring digits. Using at most `k` moves, return the smallest number you can obtain, as a string of the same length.

title: Word Wrap Minimum Slack
description: Words with lengths `lengths` must be placed in order on lines of width `W`, with one space between neighbouring words on the same line. A line holds a word sequence only if its total length (letters plus single spaces) is at most `W`. The slack of a line is `W` minus its length; the cost of a layout is the sum of `slack * slack` over every line except the last one. Return the minimum possible cost.

title: Fewest Bus Lines
description: `routes` describes bus lines as a flat list: each line is written as its stop count `k` followed by `k` distinct stop ids, e.g. `[3, 1, 2, 7, 2, 7, 9]` means line A stops at 1,2,7 and line B at 7,9. Every line runs in both directions and you may board or leave at any of its stops. Starting at stop `s`, return the fewest bus lines you must ride to reach stop `t` (`0` if `s == t`, `-1` if impossible).

examples.explanation: The fewest lines needed is 2 (-1 means impossible).
The fewest lines needed is -1 (-1 means impossible).

constraints: 1 <= number of lines <= 20, 1 <= stops per line <= 20

title: Alien Alphabet Order
description: `words` is a space-separated list of lowercase words that an alien dictionary lists in sorted order, using an unknown order of the letters. Return the alphabet order of all letters that appear in `words` (as a string) that explains the list; if several orders work return the lexicographically smallest one (in ordinary English alphabetical order of the resulting strings). Return the word `none` if no order can explain the list.
constraints: words use only the letters a-e and have length 1 to 6

title: Distinct Island Shapes
description: `grid` is an `R x C` binary table stored row by row (`1` = land). An island is a group of land cells connected up/down/left/right. Two islands have the same shape if one can be moved onto the other by sliding it (no rotation or flipping). Return the number of different island shapes.

title: Two-Ocean Flow Cells
description: `grid` is an `R x C` table of heights stored row by row. Water on a cell flows to a neighbouring cell (up/down/left/right) of equal or lower height. The top and left edges touch ocean A; the bottom and right edges touch ocean B. Return how many cells can send water to both oceans (a corner cell can touch two edges).

title: Shortest Bridge Length
description: `grid` is an `R x C` binary table stored row by row (`1` = land) that contains exactly two islands (groups of land cells connected up/down/left/right). You may turn water cells (`0`) into land. Return the minimum number of water cells that must be turned to land so that the two islands become one.

examples.explanation: A bridge of 1 cell(s) is needed.
A bridge of 2 cell(s) is needed.

constraints: each cell is 0 or 1 and there are exactly two islands

title: Cheapest Toll Route Within Time
description: `n` towns (0 to n-1) are linked by two-way roads given as flat triples `[u0, v0, minutes0, ...]`. Every time you arrive in a town (including the start, town `0`) you pay `fees[town]`, even if you pass through it again. Return the smallest total fee for a trip from town `0` to town `n - 1` that takes at most `maxTime` minutes, or `-1` if there is none.

examples.explanation: The cheapest trip costs 7 (-1 means none).
The cheapest trip costs -1 (-1 means none).

title: Longest Distinct-Label Path In Tree
description: A tree has `n` nodes (0 to n-1) and `edges` as flat pairs; `labels[i]` is the lowercase letter on node `i`. Return the largest number of nodes on a simple path in which no two neighbouring nodes on the path carry the same letter.

examples.explanation: The longest valid path has 3 node(s).
The longest valid path has 1 node(s).

constraints: edges form a tree; labels are lowercase letters

title: Rolling Ball Shortest Distance
description: `grid` is an `R x C` maze stored row by row (`0` = open, `1` = wall). A ball at `(sr, sc)` rolls in one of the four directions and keeps going until the next cell is a wall or outside the maze, then stops; only then may it choose a new direction. Return the shortest total number of cells travelled to make the ball stop exactly on `(dr, dc)`, or `-1` if impossible. The ball counts as already stopped at its starting cell.

examples.explanation: The shortest rolling distance is 14 (-1 means impossible).
The shortest rolling distance is 2 (-1 means impossible).

constraints: start and destination are open cells inside the maze

title: Remove Boxes Points
description: `boxes[i]` is the colour of the `i`-th box in a row. Repeatedly choose a block of `k >= 1` neighbouring boxes of the same colour and remove it, scoring `k * k` points; the remaining boxes close up. Return the maximum total score for removing all boxes.

title: Shortest Superstring Length
description: `words` is a space-separated list of lowercase words. Return the length of the shortest string that contains every word as a contiguous substring.

title: Time Window Maximum Replay
description: Events arrive in order of time as flat triples `(type, time, x)`. Type `0`: a reading `x` is recorded at `time`. Type `1` (with `x = 0`): ask for the largest reading whose time lies in the last `w` seconds, i.e. in `(time - w, time]`; the answer is `0` if there is none. Times never decrease. Return the sum of all answers.
constraints: 3 <= ops.length <= 300 and ops.length is a multiple of 3; 0 <= time <= 10^5, 1 <= x <= 10^4 for readings

title: Digit Product Divisible Count
description: Return how many integers `x` in `1..n` have a product of decimal digits that is divisible by `k` (a number containing the digit `0` has product `0`, which is divisible by every `k`).

title: Cheapest Product Tree
description: The array `leaves` gives the values of the leaves of a binary tree, in left-to-right order (the in-order leaf sequence). Every internal node has exactly two children, and its value is the product of the largest leaf value in its left subtree and the largest leaf value in its right subtree. Choose the tree shape that minimises the sum of all internal node values and return that sum.

title: Properly Crossing Segment Pairs
description: `segments` lists line segments as flat quadruples `[x1, y1, x2, y2, ...]`. Count the pairs of segments that cross each other properly: they meet at a single point that is strictly inside both segments (touching at an endpoint, overlapping along a line or being parallel does not count).
constraints: -100 <= coordinates <= 100; no segment is a single point

title: Largest Empty Square Among Points
description: A rectangular field spans `[0, W] x [0, H]`. `points` lists trees as flat pairs. Return the side length of the largest axis-parallel square inside the field that has no tree strictly inside it (trees on its border are allowed). The square may be placed anywhere, not only on integer positions.

examples.explanation: The largest empty square has side 5.
The largest empty square has side 3.

constraints: 0 <= x <= W, 0 <= y <= H for every tree; trees are distinct
